scenario: Startup idle, before opening any auxiliary windows

environment.build: Diagnostic Release builds; custom-protocol; ThinLTO; 16 codegen units; production frontend
environment.isolation: Separate application identifier, configuration, WebView profile and history; clipboard listener and legacy autostart cleanup disabled in both probes
environment.fixture: Same configuration and one synthetic text history item for both measurements
environment.debugger: WebView2 CDP enabled for both probes
environment.sampling: Three samples after eight seconds of startup settling; one-second intervals; median
environment.metric: Sum of Win32_PerfRawData_PerfProc_Process.WorkingSetPrivate for the native process and all descendants, divided by 1048576

native_verification.method: Real native command calls through WebView2 CDP; a diagnostic-only command calls the actual tray-menu display function; no clipboard writes or simulated paste
checks: Only clipboard, clipboardPreview and pasteQueue exist at startup
Concurrent first settings requests create one window
First settings opening receives the requested destination
Tag editor, emoji picker, text editor and permission guide receive their opening payloads
Fallback notice and tray menu cold-open successfully
Hidden auxiliary windows are reused; opening all seven leaves exactly ten windows
Destroyed tray menu is recreated and waits for its new page to become ready

limitations: Not a packaged installer benchmark or a promise of the same memory use on other machines
Memory is the complete process group, not vPaste.exe alone
Previously used auxiliary windows remain initialized for reuse; this is not idle eviction
Primary clipboard, preview and paste queue remain eager; the developer-only test room is unchanged
macOS native runtime was not available for verification
Image conversion and clipboard payload processing were not optimized in this change
